request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the

claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
All 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What changed**
- **New `rollup/RollupService.java`**: it works out each person's claimed and due-total, plus the sheet's totals, the same way the screen does. A due-total is `n/a` when none of the person's claims has a figure and no rate for their grade applies on the sheet's today. Each change takes a snapshot of these figures before it runs. After the change has written its own audit line, it compares against that snapshot and writes:
  - one `ROLLUP … person=<name> claimed=… due-total=…` line for each person whose figures moved, in the order they were added (a new person always counts as moved);
  - then `TOTALS … claimed-total=… due-total=…` if the sheet's totals moved.

  Changes that move no figure write neither line. Refused changes write nothing, because audit lines are only written once the change is saved.
- **Where it applies**: adding a claim, editing one, and changing its status; adding or editing a person; setting a rate; taking a statement; and changing the sheet's today. For the date change, `SheetService.setToday` now takes the signed-in user so the lines can name them, and the date change writes no line of its own. The figure calculation moved out of `ClaimService` into the new service; `ClaimService.figureOf` now just passes through to it.

**One change the request didn't mention but the spec requires:** a statement taken while the person's due-total is `n/a` must record `n/a`, both in the `STATEMENT` audit line and in `person-stated-total` on screen. Before this, the app recorded `0.00`. To fix it:
- a new migration, `V15__statement_due_total_none.sql`, lets the statement's due-total column be empty;
- the server stores an empty value for such statements and sends `"n/a"` in their place.

The front end needed no logic change; I only updated the comment on the `Statement` type.
